limitations: One host and one already-saved credential receipt. Public operations are modeled at quiescent boundaries, with failures before and after durable/remote effects and five explicit cancel-versus-resume await cuts. Other asynchronous interleavings remain outside this projection.

Real implementation conformance replays generated Quint traces through private filesystem receipts, loopback HTTP and the actual native-host module. Server proof verification and atomic acknowledgement/revocation are assumed. Restart reconstructs the host against unchanged persisted data; process death, fsync and multi-process coordination are outside this checker.
Progress assumes weak fairness of a successful complete cancellation retry. Permanent outages, missing retries and expired unacknowledged enrollment have no completion guarantee.

Initial challenge/PKCE issuance, MFA, Google OAuth, verified-owner activation, billing authority, account methods, and replacement credentials need separate models. A default cancel after the activation receipt has been cleared preserves the committed credential. An unconfirmed remote revocation can temporarily leave a locally selected revoked credential.

Enrollment challenge/MFA and Google state/PKCE single-use redemption, verified owner activation, ephemeral account/billing authority, one-use account mutation reviews and replacement credentials remain to be modeled.

Storage ownership and reset generations, conditional metadata admission, deletion preflight/commit atomicity, encrypted legacy upgrade and cross-process mutation lock recovery still need models. AccountCredentialGeneration covers the separate refresh compare-and-swap contract.

Eligibility health/cooldown/expiry clocks, usage refresh and mutations, priority/least-used/quota/reset strategies, and bounded-cache eviction remain to be modeled. AccountPoolAffinity covers the separate round-robin/affinity selection snapshot contract.
Consumer key revocation, durable quota reservations, settlement, restart and cross-process file locking need source-specific models.
Android pending state/expiry, acknowledgement retry budget, credential-slot ownership, cancellation and activity recreation are not covered by the Node native-host projection.
Two provider namespaces share an account id. Two one-shot refresh callers and one explicit save bound fresh generations. Atomic storage API operations and unique generation UUIDs are assumed.

Generated traces replay public APIs against actual encrypted account files. Metadata changes and deletion/replacement interleave with held refresh generations. Root ownership, process locking, storage failures, reset, conditional metadata and legacy migration require separate models.
Refresh progress assumes weak fairness of completed provider responses and the refresh commit API. Permanent provider failure is outside this projection.

Native attempt/request-id ownership, credential write-intent reservation, scoped cancellation, replacement-attempt fencing and browser pending restoration require a separate model. NativeEnrollmentRecovery covers the private host durable receipt after issuance.

OAuth state/PKCE and redirect binding, single-use enrollment claims, identity-link ownership and session/token issuance require protocol models beyond AuthStorePublication atomic storage. External provider cryptography and remote service semantics need explicit assumptions.

Round-robin with two providers, two sessions, three accounts, two concurrent calls, four total calls and one eligibility update. The same external account id exists under both providers. Selection uses captured immutable inventory and live affinity/cursor state after the expiry-write await.

Generated and specified scenario traces replay through real AccountPool.select with controlled metadata-write promises. A persistence rejection fails selection without changing affinity/cursor. The in-memory adapter does not prove encrypted storage or cross-process metadata locking; existing default-pool tests cover real storage.

Other strategies, health/time classifiers, repeated eligibility changes, usage polling, 10,000-entry eviction and credential effect admission are separate obligations. Weak fairness of selection completion is the progress assumption. There is no cancellation input in AccountPool.select.
